details: Idea E1 affine_batch: orienting on compute kernel + helpers
E2 pass1_fused_colsum: reading compute kernel + reduce/chain helpers

E1 affine_batch: 4 methods: 0 baseline per-tile (op-faithful), 1 batched (a), 2 batched+beta fold via UnaryBcast->D1 + SFPU SubBinary (b), 3 single fused chain a/b in DEST (d). DestReuseBinary has no BroadcastDim and LLK binary_dest_reuse is BroadcastType::NONE-only => FPU-exact beta fold inexpressible; SFPU sub used instead. matmul in1 index = k*N+n (row-major) confirmed in .inl

E2: reduce helper REDUCE_COL WaitUpfrontNoPop indexes ht*stride+i and chunks Wt internally by DEST_AUTO_LIMIT -> 2*cols up to 16 legal. square()=BinaryFpu Mul(x,x) (FPU, not SFPU). chain supports 2 PackTiles (distinct dst slots) with Strided (None,None) outputs. Variants: baseline / fused_copy(CopyTile+Mul, 2 packs, 1 reduce) / fused_mulone(Mul(x,ones) uniform MOP) / interleaved_ub (copy-free upper bound, not expressible in op: single-producer CB)
baseline compiled+ran; torch-ref tolerance 2e-5 too tight: FPU tf32-class operands give 5.6e-4 rel (op-documented). Relaxed sanity tol to 2e-3; gate is vs baseline output.

cols=2,Kg=1 correctness: batched bit-identical (a,b); batched_fold b max|db|=1.6e-3 (closer to torch); fused b 6.2e-3 off baseline and 2x further from torch -> precision cost. Added method 4 fused_sfpu (SFPU product+sub).
correctness sweep 10/10 pass (cols 1,2,4,5,8 x Kg 1,2); batched bit-identical everywhere; starting perf sweep

--dev unusable box-wide right now: BRISC firmware overflows region 0 (0x2270 > 0x2200) with WATCHER + PROFILE_KERNEL (tracy build); even a bare open_device probe fails. Running bench without --dev (dispatch-timeout hang detection only).

perf sweep done: focus cols=2,Kg=1 baseline 1964 ns/group -> batched 1574 (1.25x, bit-identical); cols=1 flat (1.02x); cols=8 1.54x; Kg=2 1.23-1.49x. batched_fold 1.20x (more precise, no beta_full CB); fused/fused_sfpu 1.11-1.25x, slower than batched (SFPU tile ops cost more than the CB round trip). Recommend batched.

correctness gate: fused_copy / fused_mulone / interleaved_ub bit-identical to baseline on 6 configs incl. partial scaler (hw_tail 20, 12) and cols=8 (2c=16, 2 DEST chunks); fix applied: x inputs (None,None) caller-managed because two chain elements may not both Upfront-stage one CB

sweep 1 (BLACKHOLE, single core): fused_copy REGRESSION 0.74-0.82x per chunk everywhere >=2 tiles (copy+pack of x ~110ns/tile; fused reduce also loses the square-pack / S-reduce overlap); interleaved_ub (copy-free bound) NULL 0.93-0.99x -> one wide reduce is not cheaper than two narrow ones; dest_acc_xsq (option b) WIN 1.17x focus r2c2, 1.36x r4, 1.55x r8, flat r1 -- but not bit-identical (Float32 qf tile through FPU SrcA: rel 1.4e-3 vs baseline 4e-4) and needs a fallback for the hw_tail chunk. Next: add fallback + AccumulateViaAdd (SFPU fp32) Q reduce variant.

sweep 2 (BLACKHOLE, 6 variants x 20 geometries, one fresh run per cell, focus 3x median) reproduces sweep 1 within noise: fused_copy 0.76-0.83x, fused_mulone 0.69-0.78x, interleaved_ub 0.93-1.0x, dest_acc_xsq 1.17x focus / 1.38x r4 / 1.55x r8 / flat r1 (rel vs fp64 1.4e-3 vs baseline 4e-4), dest_acc_xsq_sfpu 1.13x / 1.34x / 1.52x, 0.91-0.94x at r1 c>=4 (rel 7e-4). Report written to sweep_report.md

E2 verdicts: (a) fused [x|xsq] chain + one reduce = REGRESSION 0.76x focus (mechanism: forced x copy+pack ~110ns/tile and loss of square-pack/S-reduce overlap; wide reduce not cheaper than two narrow ones). (b) dest_acc_xsq = WIN 1.17x focus, 1.38x r4, 1.55x r8, flat r1, precision cost rel 1.4e-3 vs 4e-4 (FPU SrcA truncation of Float32 partial sums); (b-prime) SFPU Q reduce 1.13x/1.34x/1.52x with rel 7e-4. hw_tail chunk keeps baseline path. Artifacts under perf_experiments/pass1_fused_colsum (bench, test, README, sweep_report.md). Nothing committed; real op untouched.
